To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the translation of Object-Z specifications to FDR input notation is feasible, that the translation of the Object-Z specification of the Dining Philosophers problem to FDR input is more difficult than the translation of other Object-Z specifications, and that the resulting FDR input specifications of the Dining Philosophes problem are more difficult to model check than the resulting FDR specifications of other Object-Z classes.
(a) a direct translation from Object-Z classes to FDR input is not efficient, (b) a translation that is based on the translation of the class invariant to a CSP process is not efficient either, and

(1) the translation scheme that is based on the CSP notion of a state machine is more efficient than the translation scheme that uses CSP processes, (2) the translation scheme based on the CSP notions of a state machine and a process is more efficient than a scheme that is based solely on the CSP notion a process, and (3) the translation scheme is more efficient than any other scheme we investigated

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, for the examples investigated, the best translation scheme was the one that preserved the Object-Z syntax as much as possible, and that this was the scheme that could be model checked most efficiently.
there is no single translation scheme that can be recommended for all Object-Z class specifications.

there is no single best way to translate Object-Z classes to CSP, but that the best translation depends on the size of the class, the number of instances of the class in the specification, and the number of instances in the model.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the translation scheme proposed in this paper can model check Object-Z specifications with significantly fewer state spaces than the translation scheme in [10] and that the resulting state spaces are significantly smaller than the original Object-Z specification.
the translation scheme that we propose is more efficient, and in some cases much more efficient, than the one used by the FDR tool.
the Object-Z to CSP translation is a viable method for model checking Object-Z specifications.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the translation scheme is crucial for the efficiency of the model checking process.

the Object-Z translation scheme presented by Utting et al. (2011) is a good compromise between the preservation of the semantics of the Object-Z specification, and how efficiently it can be model checked with FDR.
, in the case of the Object-Z class of specifications, the translation scheme that performs best is one that preserves the structure of the original specification.
